sources.entry: RERO ILS - Large-scale ILS that can be run as a service with consortial features, intended primarily for library networks. Includes most standard modules (circulation, acquisitions, cataloging,...) and a web-based public and professional interface. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: RERO ILS is an open source, web-based integrated library system built for library networks and consortia, covering circulation, cataloguing, acquisitions and a public online catalog.
summary.what_it_does: RERO ILS manages library networks or independent libraries, covering document acquisition, circulation, cataloguing and search. It provides a consortial model with configuration at organization and library levels. The cataloguing editor follows RDA and BibFrame standards, with management of periodicals, subscriptions and issue predictions. A public online catalog offers search and filtering, customizable views per organization and library, and integration of external resources such as ebooks and databases. The circulation module handles check-out, check-in, item requests, interlibrary loans and patron management. Bibliographic data is exposed as JSON in the BibFrame model through an API.
use_cases: heritage, public or school library software
how_to_run: See the installation documentation referenced in the README for production deployment
See the developer documentation referenced in the README for a development environment
Frontend requires the separate rero-ils-ui repository (ng-core based)
A MEF (Multilingual Entity File) server is required: use RERO's public MEF server or run your own
notable: Consortial model designed for library networks with organization and library configuration levels
Cataloguing aligned with RDA and BibFrame
Multilingual authority file (MEF) aggregating IdRef and GND, aligned through VIAF
Bibliographic data available as JSON via API
In production since 2021 at RERO+ and UCLouvain networks
caveats: Requires substantial configuration or development effort to self-host, per the README
Needs a MEF authority server, either RERO's public one or self-hosted
Frontend and backend are split across three repositories including rero-ils-ui and MEF
keywords: run a library for my team
